full_judgment:
5. Against the said judgment and decree of the learned Assistant Judge, the defendant-petitioners preferred Other Appeal No. 39 of 2005 before the District Judge, Rangpur. The learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Rangpur who heard the appeal by his judgment and decree dated 28-9-2006 allowed the same and dismissed the suit on the findings, inter alia, that in view of the provisions of section 95A of the Act, the transaction in question became past and closed, so the same could not be treated as one under section 60 of the Transfer of Property Act and thus to maintain the suit for redemption of the mortgage property; in view of the finding of the trial Court that the mortgagee delivered back possession of the mortgaged property to the mortgagors 46 years before on receipt of the kabala money, plaintiffs suit for “রাইট টু রিডাস্পশন" was not maintainable in law and the only remedy open to them was to file a suit for declaration of title and for recovery of khas possession. The appellate Court further found that the finding of the trial Court that the predecessor of the plaintiffs took possession of the suit land immediately after returning back the kabala money to the predecessor of the defendants was based on misinterpretation of the deposition of the plaintiffs witnesses as well as their evidence in cross-examination. 

 11. The Appellate Court being the last Court of fact considering the evidence in detail came to the finding that the plaintiffs failed to prove their case by examining the competent witnesses whereas, the defendants proved their case as made out in the written statement. The Appellate Court came to the further finding that the trial Court ought to have decided that the plaintiffs suit without prayer for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was not maintainable in law. The Appellate Court also found that the trial Court on wrong interpretation of the witnesses of the plaintiffs came to the wrong finding that the price of the suit land was returned back to the plaintiffs predecessor. The Appellate Court further came to the finding that as per their own case, the mortgage having been redeemed 46 years ago, the trial Court erred in decreeing the suit.
